first_impression.reaction: Okay, the first line is a bit poetic for a train scroll, but by the second paragraph I can see which places are wet and New Zealand is 'the plain spring choice'. The Key Takeaways list all ten, so I stayed. I read the takeaways, skipped down to the table and the 'Where is warm' FAQ, then left. Might bookmark it. Wouldn't enquire yet.

journey.quote: For couples weighing wedding destinations, November is a month of edges.
journey.reaction: What does 'a month of edges' even mean? I searched for places, just tell me where.

journey.quote: New Zealand is the plain spring choice.
journey.reaction: Now that's a direct answer. More of this, earlier.

journey.quote: This list covers the Greek islands, Portugal, the Amalfi Coast, the French Riviera and Hawaii in the northern autumn, and New Zealand, Mauritius, the Seychelles, Fiji and Bali in the southern spring and early summer.
journey.reaction: Good, all ten in one line, split by hemisphere. This is what I came for.

journey.quote: Pick the November trade-off you can live with, whether that is a quieter European coast, a changeable New Zealand spring or a tropical island at the start of its rains.
journey.reaction: Fair, but it doesn't tell me there's a comparison table further down. I only found it by scrolling a long way.

journey.section: How we chose these ten November destinations
journey.quote: Base periods and the way a rain day is counted differ from country to country, and the WMO asks for care when city climates are set side by side, so read each figure on its own.
journey.reaction: This is a footnote, not something I need before the list. Skipped.

journey.quote: The Hellenic National Meteorological Service's figures for Naxos, for which HNMS publishes no base period, give a November minimum monthly temperature of 13.7°C, a monthly mean of 16.4°C and a maximum of 18.8°C.
journey.reaction: The numbers are useful but I have to wade through who published what to get them. On a phone this reads like a report.

journey.quote: Lisbon's climate normals for 1961 to 1990, supplied by IPMA
journey.reaction: 1961 to 1990? Is this still true in 2026? At least it's honest about it.

journey.quote: As at November 2026, Smartraveller gives the cyclone season as November to May and warns that the airport may close during a cyclone.
journey.reaction: Dated and specific. That's the kind of thing I trust.

journey.quote: | Fiji | Start of the wet and cyclone season (FMS, November 2025) | Cyclones and flash flooding |
journey.reaction: The table is the best bit of the page for me. Shame it sits after all ten long sections.

journey.quote: Weigh them against your guest list with Wedded Concierge.
journey.reaction: I don't know who you are. Is Wedded Concierge a person, a form, a paid service? It's never explained at this point.

journey.quote: The Indian Ocean islands. Mauritius records a November mean daily maximum of 30.2°C at Port Louis (normals for 1971 to 2000), and the Seychelles 30.3°C at Victoria (normals for 1981 to 2010).
journey.reaction: Straight answer to a question I actually had. This should be higher up.

journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD and confirms each venue's inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Quotes in AUD. I'm in Singapore, so this tells me the site is for Australians, not really me.

unanswered_questions: Roughly how much does a November wedding cost in any of these places, and is November cheaper than peak season?
If I had to pick one or two, which does the site actually recommend for November?
Do you work with couples who are not based in Australia?
What is Wedded Concierge exactly, and is there a fee to talk to someone?

turn_offs_found.quote: For couples weighing wedding destinations, November is a month of edges.
turn_offs_found.why: The opening line is atmosphere, not an answer. I nearly bounced.

turn_offs_found.quote: The page sets no threshold for a rain day, and November tops its rainfall column.
turn_offs_found.why: Methodology notes inside every weather block make each section slow to scan on a phone.
The most useful summary is buried after ten long sections, and the takeaways don't point to it.

would_share_with: A friend who has just got engaged and keeps saying 'somewhere warm in November'

cta_reaction.quote: Tell us your November date, your guest numbers and who will need extra care on the journey through Wedded Concierge.
cta_reaction.why: I came for a quick answer and I don't know the brand yet. I'd bookmark, maybe click the Bali or New Zealand guide, but I'm not handing over my date and guest numbers on the first visit, especially when nothing says what the service is or what it costs.

top_3_changes: Make the first sentence an answer. OLD: "For couples weighing wedding destinations, November is a month of edges. North of the equator it is late autumn, and southern Europe is winding down its season." NEW: "Where you marry in November comes down to which hemisphere you choose. North of the equator it is late autumn, and southern Europe is winding down its season."

Point skimmers to the table from the takeaways. OLD: "- Pick the November trade-off you can live with, whether that is a quieter European coast, a changeable New Zealand spring or a tropical island at the start of its rains." NEW: "- Pick the November trade-off you can live with, whether that is a quieter European coast, a changeable New Zealand spring or a tropical island at the start of its rains. The at-a-glance table below compares all ten in one view."

Say what Wedded Concierge is at first mention. OLD: "Weigh them against your guest list with [Wedded Concierge](/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=wedding-destinations-november&utm_content=primary)." NEW: "Weigh them against your guest list with our planners at [Wedded Concierge](/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=wedding-destinations-november&utm_content=primary)."

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Priya, a phone-on-the-train search visitor who doesn't know the brand
No invented brand facts; missing info listed as unanswered questions
Suggested edits add no prices, venue names, statistics, business details or new weather facts
VERIFY markers and HTML comments treated as invisible
Suggested edits use Australian English and no em dashes

assumptions: Quotes containing markdown links are given as rendered text (link text only), as a reader would see them; the suggested-edit old strings keep the exact markdown source.
'Our planners' in edit 3 relies on the draft's own statement 'We plan weddings in all ten' and adds no new business detail.
Persona is provisional (search intent proxy), so reactions reflect search intent rather than calibrated GSC data.

open_questions.question: Should the at-a-glance table move up (straight after Key takeaways) for search visitors, or is a pointer in the takeaways enough?
Is the AUD and Australian-guest framing intended to exclude non-Australian searchers, or should one line say who the service is for?
